definition: to be a sign of something or to show that it exists

collocations.example: Red flashing lights usually denote danger on the road.
A rising line can denote a change in temperature.

definition: a small hollow mark made in a hard surface by a knock or pressure

collocations.example: The accident left a deep dent in the fender.
A stray ball can make a dent in the roof.

definition: relating to the teeth or to the care of teeth

collocations.example: I have a dental appointment at three o'clock today.
Good dental hygiene helps prevent gum disease and decay.

definition: to force a foreigner to leave a country, usually because they have no legal right to stay

collocations.example: The government plans to deport thousands of illegal immigrants.
Authorities will deport him back to his home country.

definition: the natural process by which a substance is gradually laid down in a layer

collocations.example: Sediment deposition slowly built up the river delta.
Mineral deposition formed thick layers inside the cave.

definition: to remove government rules and controls from a business or industry

collocations.example: The government decided to deregulate the airline industry.
Officials voted to deregulate prices in the energy market.

definition: to speak about someone or something in a scornful, mocking way

collocations.example: Critics were quick to deride the new proposal.
Opponents deride the plan as a waste of money.

definition: to dislike and feel contempt for someone or something very strongly

collocations.example: She came to despise him for his constant lies.
Many people despise dishonesty in their close friends.

definition: harm or damage caused to something

collocations.example: He worked long hours to the detriment of his health.
The changes were made without detriment to overall performance.

definition: to make someone or something seem less important or less worthy of respect

collocations.example: They spread rumors to devalue her work unfairly.
Such comments devalue the contribution of every volunteer.

definition: differing from what is considered normal or socially acceptable

collocations.example: Teachers quickly noticed the student's deviant behavior in class.
The group was labeled socially deviant by its critics.

definition: going in a slanting direction, joining two opposite corners

collocations.example: She drew a diagonal line across the page.
His shirt had bold diagonal stripes across the front.

definition: a form of a language spoken in a particular region or by a particular group

collocations.example: It was hard to understand the local dialect.
She still speaks in a strong regional dialect.

definition: any of the written numbers from 0 to 9

collocations.example: Please enter the final single digit of your code.
The country suffered years of double-digit inflation.

definition: to treat something unworthy as if it deserved serious attention or respect

collocations.example: I refuse to dignify that rumor with a response.
She would not dignify the rude question with an answer.

definition: working hard and carefully, giving proper attention to a task

collocations.example: She is a diligent worker who rarely makes mistakes.
Please be more diligent in checking your figures.

definition: an official document showing that someone has completed a course of study

collocations.example: He finally earned his high school diploma last year.
She hung her college diploma on the office wall.

definition: extremely serious, bad, or urgent

collocations.example: The refugees are in dire need of clean water.
Ignoring the warning could have dire consequences for everyone.

definition: a person who follows and believes in the teachings of a leader or teacher

collocations.example: He was a devoted disciple of the famous philosopher.
The loyal disciple recorded every word his teacher spoke.

definition: a club or party where people dance to recorded popular music

collocations.example: Friday is always disco night at the student union.
They decided to go to the disco after dinner.

definition: to break the connection between two things, especially to a power source or network

collocations.example: Remember to disconnect from the network before leaving.
Please disconnect the cable before moving the computer.

definition: a feeling of unhappiness because you are not satisfied with your situation

collocations.example: There is widespread discontent among the factory workers.
He chose to express his discontent by resigning quietly.

definition: to make people stop respecting or believing in someone or something

collocations.example: His political rivals tried hard to discredit him publicly.
New evidence helped discredit the old theory completely.

definition: separate and clearly distinct from other things

collocations.example: Language is built from many discrete units of sound.
The survey data falls into several discrete categories.

definition: a feeling that someone or something is unworthy of your respect

collocations.example: She looked at the cheap gift with disdain.
He made no secret of his disdain for authority.

definition: not honest; intending to cheat, lie, or deceive people

collocations.example: I never expected such a dishonest person among us.
Her answer was deliberately dishonest and quite misleading.

definition: a feeling of disappointment when you learn something is not as good as you believed

collocations.example: There is growing disillusion with the whole political system.
A deep sense of disillusion followed the election results.

definition: making you feel sad or depressed; gloomy and dreary

collocations.example: The dismal weather ruined our outdoor plans completely.
The dismal, gray sky hung over the deserted town.

definition: a large or unfair difference between two or more things

collocations.example: There is a wide disparity between rich and poor.
The disparity between the two regions keeps on growing.

definition: a lack of proper balance between two things in size or amount

collocations.example: There is a clear disproportion between effort and reward.
There is a clear disproportion in the number of men and women.

definition: to stop someone from taking part in or being eligible for something

collocations.example: A serious injury could disqualify him from the race.
The committee voted to disqualify the candidate for cheating.

definition: a lack of care, attention, or respect for something

collocations.example: He showed a reckless disregard for his own safety.
She acted with total disregard for other people's feelings.

definition: to spread information or ideas widely to many people

collocations.example: The agency works to disseminate information to the public.
Workshops help disseminate knowledge among team members quickly.

definition: a person who publicly opposes the official policy of a government

collocations.example: The famous political dissident was finally released from prison.
A small dissident group organized the peaceful protest.

definition: a feeling of dislike for something you find unpleasant or offensive

collocations.example: She has a strong distaste for office politics.
He pushed the plate away with obvious distaste.

definition: to reduce something to its essential meaning or most important parts

collocations.example: The author managed to distil his ideas into one article.
The book tries to distil the essence of good leadership.

definition: a feeling that you cannot trust or rely on someone or something

collocations.example: There is deep distrust between the two neighboring countries.
Public distrust of politicians has grown in recent years.

definition: an animal like a small horse with long ears, used for carrying loads

collocations.example: The children took turns to ride a donkey.
The stubborn donkey refused to cross the narrow bridge.

definition: a building where students live and sleep at a school or college

collocations.example: She lived in a crowded college dormitory for years.
They raced back to the dormitory building before curfew.

definition: a thick mixture of flour and liquid, used for baking bread or pastry

collocations.example: The baker began to knead the dough slowly.
Roll out the dough until it is very thin.

definition: a white or gray bird often used as a symbol of peace

collocations.example: A white dove was released at the ceremony.
The artist painted a dove of peace above the city.

definition: a feature of something that makes it less useful or acceptable; a disadvantage

collocations.example: The high cost is the major drawback of this plan.
The only drawback of the apartment was its size.

definition: a tube or channel that carries air, liquid, or wires from one place to another

collocations.example: Cold air flows through the air duct into each room.
Dust had collected inside the old heating duct.

definition: a model of a human figure used for display or testing

collocations.example: Engineers placed a crash-test dummy in the driver's seat.
The shop dummy wore the latest winter coat.

definition: a hill of sand formed by the wind near a beach or in a desert

collocations.example: We climbed to the top of the sand dune.
A towering dune blocked our view of the sea.

definition: to gradually become smaller in size, amount, or number

collocations.example: Their savings slowly began to dwindle away.
The wild herds continue to dwindle in number.

definition: a series of rulers who all belong to the same family

collocations.example: The ancient royal dynasty ruled for three hundred years.
The ruling dynasty collapsed after years of civil war.

definition: all the living things in an area and the way they affect each other and their environment

collocations.example: Pollution threatens the fragile ecosystem of the lake.
Logging has damaged the natural ecosystem of the forest.

definition: strange and frightening in a mysterious way

collocations.example: An eerie silence fell over the empty house.
She had an eerie feeling of being watched.

definition: oldest of three or more people, especially in a family

collocations.example: Their eldest son is studying law at university.
His eldest daughter will inherit the family business.

definition: the quality of being graceful and stylish in appearance or manner

collocations.example: She carried herself with great elegance and grace.
The room was decorated with simple, casual elegance.

definition: able to speak or write fluently and in a persuasive, expressive way

collocations.example: He gave an eloquent speech at the dinner.
She is an eloquent speaker who moves every audience.

definition: to come out from a source; to flow or spread from somewhere

collocations.example: A strange smell seemed to emanate from the basement.
You could feel the heat emanate from the furnace.

definition: an official order that stops trade with another country

collocations.example: The trade embargo hurt the small island economy.
The council voted to impose an embargo on weapons.

definition: famous, respected, and admired within a particular profession

collocations.example: The lecture was given by an eminent scientist.
She became an eminent figure in modern architecture.

definition: the ability to understand and share the feelings of another person

collocations.example: Good nurses show empathy toward their frightened patients.
He felt genuine empathy for the struggling families.

definition: expressing something in a strong and very clear way

collocations.example: The minister issued an emphatic denial of the charges.
She was emphatic about finishing the project on time.

definition: to try to equal or match someone by imitating what they do

collocations.example: Many young players try hard to emulate their heroes.
Other firms now seek to emulate his success.

definition: to please someone greatly; to charm and delight them

collocations.example: The young singer managed to enchant the whole audience.
These old fairy tales still enchant young children.

definition: to change information into a particular form so it can be stored or sent

collocations.example: The brain works hard to encode new information.
Spies used a cipher to encode the secret message.

definition: to attract someone by offering something pleasant or advantageous

collocations.example: Low prices are used to entice new customers.
They tried to entice him into joining the club.

definition: to establish something so firmly that it is very hard to change

collocations.example: The policy may entrench divisions between the two sides.
The reforms helped the party entrench its own power.

definition: to consider one thing to be the same as or equal to another

collocations.example: Do not equate great wealth with true happiness.
People often wrongly equate old age with wisdom.

definition: fair and reasonable, treating everyone in an equal way

collocations.example: They sought a more equitable distribution of wealth.
Both sides hoped for an equitable solution to the dispute.

definition: not having one clear meaning; open to more than one interpretation

collocations.example: She gave an equivocal answer to avoid trouble.
The committee remained equivocal about the new proposal.

definition: to get rid of something completely; to destroy it entirely

collocations.example: Doctors are fighting hard to eradicate the disease.
The charity works to eradicate poverty in rural areas.

definition: to make a mistake or do something wrong

collocations.collocation: err on the side of caution
collocations.example: Doctors often err on the side of caution.
Even experienced leaders sometimes err in judgment.

definition: respect and admiration for someone or something

collocations.example: She is held in high esteem by her colleagues.
The whole town holds the old doctor in esteem.

definition: to cut lines or a design into a hard surface using acid or a tool

collocations.example: The factory can etch tiny circuits onto the chip.
Craftsmen etch a delicate design into the glass.

definition: time that has no end; a period that seems to last forever

collocations.example: He promised to love her for eternity.
The wait at the clinic felt like an eternity.

definition: a type of alcohol made from plants, often used as a fuel

collocations.example: Many cars can now run on ethanol fuel.
Factories use corn to produce ethanol quite cheaply.

definition: the unit of money used in many countries of the European Union

collocations.example: The dollar fell sharply against the euro today.
Tourists can pay in euros at most shops.

definition: to escape or avoid someone or something, often by being clever

collocations.example: The thief managed to evade capture for months.
The minister tried to evade the difficult question.

definition: to legally force someone to leave a property they are living in

collocations.example: The landlord threatened to evict the tenants immediately.
Police arrived to evict the squatters from the building.

definition: to annoy or frustrate someone very much

collocations.example: The constant noise began to exasperate the teacher.
His endless excuses exasperate everyone in the office.

definition: to be extremely good at doing something

collocations.example: Her children all excel at sports and music.
He hopes to excel in international business someday.

definition: a government tax on certain goods produced and sold within a country

collocations.example: The government raised the excise duty on cigarettes.
There is a heavy excise on imported alcohol.

definition: a short trip made for pleasure, especially by a group of people

collocations.example: The whole class will go on an excursion tomorrow.
They enjoyed a pleasant excursion along the coast.

definition: a person or thing that is a perfect or typical example of something

collocations.example: The building is an exemplar of modern design.
Her essay is a perfect exemplar of clear writing.

definition: to be a typical example of something, or to show it clearly

collocations.example: These athletes exemplify the values of teamwork and discipline.
These three cases clearly exemplify the wider problem.

definition: to make someone feel very happy, excited, and full of energy

collocations.example: Thrill rides are designed to exhilarate the riders.
The steep descent can both exhilarate and terrify you.

definition: able to be explained or understood

collocations.example: His strange behavior is not easily explicable.
The results are explicable in terms of simple physics.

definition: spending or costing much more money than is necessary or reasonable

collocations.example: She scandalized her family with her extravagant lifestyle.
His extravagant tastes quickly emptied his bank account.

definition: to invent false information in order to deceive people

collocations.example: It angers me that people fabricate a story like that.
The officer was accused of trying to fabricate evidence.

definition: one particular part or aspect of something

collocations.example: The caste system shapes nearly every facet of life.
Let us now examine another facet of the problem.

definition: a fast bird of prey with long pointed wings, sometimes trained to hunt

collocations.example: The peregrine falcon dived steeply toward its prey.
The hunter released his trained falcon into the sky.

definition: to lose strength or confidence and stop being firm or steady

collocations.example: The economic recovery could begin to falter soon.
Even strong leaders can falter under intense pressure.

definition: a serious shortage of food affecting a large number of people

collocations.example: The long drought caused widespread famine across the region.
Charities rushed famine relief to the stricken villages.

definition: a person who is extremely enthusiastic about a particular interest

collocations.example: She is a non-smoking, non-drinking fitness fanatic.
My younger brother is a complete sports fanatic.

definition: an impressive achievement that needs great skill, strength, or courage

collocations.example: Crossing the desert alone was a remarkable feat.
The new bridge is a great feat of engineering.

definition: very weak and lacking physical strength

collocations.example: A feeble voice answered from the dark room.
The old and feeble man could barely walk.

definition: to cut down a tree so that it falls to the ground

collocations.example: The workers were hired to fell trees in the forest.
He learned to fell timber with an old axe.

definition: the belief that women should have the same rights and opportunities as men

collocations.example: She wrote several essays about radical feminism.
The book traces the rise of feminism in America.

definition: a green plant with feathery leaves and no flowers, found in damp places

collocations.example: A single fern leaf uncurled in the morning light.
Lush ferns covered the floor of the rainforest.

definition: the quality of being loyal and faithful to a person, promise, or belief

collocations.example: He strongly believed in lifelong marital fidelity.
People have failed to act in fidelity to their vows.
